title: Heat Reduces How Cyclists Use Carbohydrate
paragraphs: Athletes often eat or drink carbohydrates during long exercise because their muscles need energy. A new study in the Journal of Physiology looked at what happens to this energy when it is very hot.

Researchers asked 17 cyclists to ride a stationary bike for 90 minutes. They did two rides in a room at 40 degrees and one ride at 20 degrees. Before the second hot ride, the cyclists practised in the heat for nine days. The scientists used blood tests and small muscle samples to follow the sugar.

In hot conditions, the cyclists used about 27 percent less of the carbohydrate they drank. Nine days of heat practice did not change this. The lead author says athletes should not eat less carbohydrate in the heat, but they should still drink enough water. The study was small.

questions.q: What was the temperature in the hot rides?
How much less carbohydrate did the cyclists use in the heat?
What advice does the lead author give?
questions.a: Do not eat less carbohydrate in the heat, and drink enough water.
